title: Orcel Agent: Core-integration planner (DeerFlow-derived MCP client), milestones M2 and M3
objective: Turn the M1 Orcel Agent (apps/orcel-agent: a standard-library MCP client of the Orcel edge with a scripted planner) into a planner that can drive a LangChain chat model, using copied and adapted DeerFlow 2.0 middlewares (loop detection, todos, compaction, tool-output budget, error and dangling-call recovery, clarification) and LangGraph checkpoints, while it stays an unprivileged client: every tool comes from the Orcel edge and every call is authorized, executed and audited by orceld. M2 and M3 of the adopted plan (docs/orcel/implementation-readiness/prep/DEERFLOW_ORCEL_AGENT_MASTER_PLAN.md). Activation packet: docs/orcel/implementation-readiness/prep/SG-000129.md.

include: Activate the SG-000129 contract only. Every slice below needs its own exact-head qualified implementation PR with a fresh-context security judge.

Slice 1 (M2, dependency admission): a hash-locked Python dependency set for apps/orcel-agent only (langchain, langchain-core, langgraph, langgraph-checkpoint, langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite and their transitive closure), installed wheels-only with --require-hashes into an isolated environment; a transitive license table; a hash-pinned advisory audit; LangSmith, OpenTelemetry and every other tracer forced off before any LangChain import; no tiktoken, no provider SDK, no SQLite loadable extension; an egress-denied test; the MIT notice at apps/orcel-agent/third_party/deer-flow/LICENSE and a provenance ledger. mcp and langchain-mcp-adapters are not admitted in slice 1.

Slice 2 (M2, planner adapter and orchestration): a LangChain chat-model Planner adapter behind the M1 Planner protocol, and MCP tool-call orchestration whose every dispatch goes through the M1 gate and its stdlib edge session (allowlist, approval budget, refusal-is-final, step budget, resume invariant). The agent's entry point refuses any allowlist that is not a subset of the M1 read-only set. Tests use only LangChain's in-process fake chat models (labelled scripted); scripted parity with M1 on BM-02 Tier A.

Slice 3 (M2, loop detection): ADAPT DeerFlow's loop-detection middleware (the detection core unchanged in logic, with Orcel tool names; the integration through ChatModelPlanner) and port its detection-core tests.

Slice 4 (M3, context middlewares): todos and task decomposition (LangChain's TodoListMiddleware plus DeerFlow's delta), summarization (the LangChain built-in plus DeerFlow's hooks), the tool-output budget and synopsis (in memory, or only in the private store), tool-error handling and dangling-call repair mapped to the resume invariant, and clarification (a question is never consent).

Slice 5 (M3, persistent planning): LangGraph SQLite checkpoints for plan and message state inside the private per-run store, under the M1 store rules as widened by the recorded store decision, plus an explicit owner-only protected DACL on Windows; kill-and-resume tests.

Slice 6 (evaluation): BM-02 Tier A and the synthetic middleware tasks (loop trap, long context, oversized output, injected instructions, kill and resume) through the agent against M1, reporting success, refusals, latency, peak memory, context growth, recovery and security failures; every row labelled deterministic-scripted.
exclude: Any change to orceld, its policy, approval broker, leases, journal, hosts or providers; any new MCP tool, argument, profile or edge behaviour.
DeerFlow sandboxes (local, AIO, E2B, OpenSandbox, Boxlite, Kubernetes), bash, file, browser and computer-control tools, and any other path that executes, reads or writes outside the Orcel edge.
DeerFlow's gateway, auth, channels, scheduler, persistence, frontend and telemetry; any listener or network client other than the stdio pipe to the edge.
Mutating or approval-bearing tools in the agent allowlist: it stays the M1 read-only set until a read-only lease-state signal exists under a separately decided change.
Model inference with real weights, model or tokenizer downloads, and hosted model providers (M4, founder decision 2).
Runtime skill installation, memory and subagents (M6), packaging, exposure, Control Room integration and release (M7).
Running the agent against an orceld that may hold a Full User or Admin lease; tests use a test orceld only.

authority_delta.activation: None. Activating SG-000129 lets its slices be implemented and proven under the founder decision; the activation itself adds no dependency, donor code, tool, listener or authority.
authority_delta.orceld: None. orceld, its policy, approval broker, leases, journal, hosts and providers are unchanged; the agent is one more MCP client.
authority_delta.mcp: None. No MCP tool, argument, profile or edge behaviour changes; the agent keeps its M1 read-only allowlist.
authority_delta.approval: Unchanged rules: every approval is asked by orceld's broker of the person; the agent never sees, mints, caches or relays an approval or lease, keeps its per-run approval budget, and stops at the first denial.
authority_delta.dependencies: Proposed only (slice 1): a hash-locked, wheels-only Python dependency set for apps/orcel-agent only (LangChain and LangGraph; mcp and langchain-mcp-adapters are not admitted unless slice 2 records a need), with a license table and a pinned advisory audit; nothing in orceld, the edge or any shipped artifact depends on it.
authority_delta.donor_code: Proposed only (slices 2 to 5): copied or adapted MIT-licensed DeerFlow 2.0 middleware code under apps/orcel-agent, with provenance headers, the verbatim license and a ledger; no execution, sandbox, tool or network code.
authority_delta.agent_state: Proposed only (slice 5): plan and message checkpoints (which contain tool results, so file and UIA text) inside the private per-run store, a recorded widening of M1's journal-only content rule; owner-only, size-capped including SQLite sidecars, expiring, deleted on completion.
authority_delta.network: None. No socket or listener; LangSmith and every tracer stay off and an egress-denied test enforces it.
authority_delta.process: None. The agent still spawns exactly one child, the built edge.
authority_delta.privileged: None. SG-000096 Full User shell remains unarmed.

decisions.question: Open the governed change
decisions.decision: Founder decision of 2026-10-30, given in the implementing session's chat and recorded verbatim on issue #536. Authorization: "I reaffirm my founder authorization to copy, adapt, refactor, and rebrand appropriately licensed DeerFlow 2.0 code for Orcel. You are authorized to initiate the formal SpecGrain activation process for: Orcel Agent — Core-integration planner (DeerFlow-derived MCP client). Use the adopted architecture in: docs/orcel/implementation-readiness/prep/DEERFLOW_ORCEL_AGENT_MASTER_PLAN.md. Prepare the complete activation specification, security analysis, dependency admission, acceptance tests, and independent review. Do not treat this instruction alone as a completed SpecGrain activation. Activate the grain only after satisfying the repository's formal governance and decision requirements." Implementation: "Prioritize M2 and M3 once their governance requirements are satisfied." and "Once the required governance gates are satisfied, begin the first executable M2 implementation immediately." The items to "Implement or transplant" are listed as: "LangChain-compatible planner adapter", "DeerFlow loop detection", "MCP tool-call orchestration", "Todo and task-decomposition middleware", "Context compaction and summarization", "Tool-output budgeting", "Error handling and dangling-call recovery", "Persistent planning and checkpoints". Boundaries: "The agent is an unprivileged MCP client." "orceld remains the sole execution and approval authority." "Do not import DeerFlow's unrestricted host-shell tools, alternative computer-control paths, cloud sandbox backends, or other privileged mechanisms that could bypass Orcel's broker." "Keep the agent unexposed and unshipped during this phase." "No runtime skill installation, unexpected network egress, approval bypass, or Full User lease assumptions." "No model inference or downloads without separately satisfying the model-selection and licensing gates." Process: "Continue without routine confirmation requests."

decisions.question: Sequencing
decisions.decision: SG-000129 runs as an additional active grain beside SG-000096, SG-000127 and SG-000128. It touches only apps/orcel-agent, tests/benchmarks and the agent's CI job, which none of them touch.

decisions.question: Rule change: the lawful open-grain set
decisions.decision: The canonical open-grain rule (apps/orcel-mcp/src/openai-plugin.test.ts and p20-architecture.test.ts) allowed SG-000096, SG-000127 and SG-000128 together. It now also allows SG-000096, SG-000127, SG-000128 and SG-000129 together, only while CURRENT.md records SG-000129's founder decision, the parallel grains SG-000108, SG-000120 and SG-000126 stay closed, and no other grain beyond SG-000096 exists. This follows the SG-000128 precedent (issue #515). The other rule changes are recorded separately below (the private store and the source scan).

decisions.question: Dependency versions
decisions.decision: Start from the versions the DeerFlow pin 81e1ab8 resolves in its backend/uv.lock (langchain 1.3.14, langchain-core 1.4.9, langgraph 1.2.9, langgraph-checkpoint 4.3.0, langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite 3.1.2, langgraph-prebuilt 1.1.0, pydantic 2.13.3; the pin also resolves mcp 1.30.0 and langchain-mcp-adapters 0.2.2, which are not admitted in slice 1), because the copied middlewares subclass those LangChain built-ins and were tested against them. A version moves only to fix a recorded advisory or a test failure, and every move is recorded in the lock's notes. Every admitted package must be under an OSI-approved permissive license (MIT, BSD, Apache-2.0, PSF, ISC) or be recorded and reviewed in the license table before admission.

decisions.question: Use DeerFlow's agent factory or a thin loop
decisions.decision: A thin loop on LangChain's create_agent with the copied self-contained middlewares; DeerFlow's agents/factory.py (a 101k-line import closure with sandbox defaulting to true) is not imported. Superseded by the slice 3 decision: the M1 loop stays the only dispatcher and the copied middlewares run through the planner; DeerFlow's factory is still not imported.

decisions.question: Who holds the MCP session
decisions.decision: Only the M1 gate's stdlib client holds the edge session. LangChain tools handed to the model are thin proposals that call the gate. No mcp or langchain-mcp-adapters session, client or tool may exist in the agent; slice 2 converts the edge's tool schemas itself. The extended source scan and its denylist pin this.

decisions.question: Rule change: what the agent's private store may hold
decisions.decision: M1's store holds only the dispatch journal: tool names, argument digests and error codes, never tool results or file content (orcel_agent/store.py). Slice 5 widens this: LangGraph checkpoints hold plan and message state, which includes tool results and so file and UIA text. The widening is allowed only with: the checkpoint database and every SQLite sidecar (-wal, -shm, -journal) inside the run directory and counted against the size cap, where the cap counts the database pages, the WAL and any rollback journal together: PRAGMA max_page_count bounds the database, journal_size_limit and a WAL checkpoint bound the WAL and journal, and a capacity check of the real file sizes runs before each checkpoint is saved, so filling past the cap fails closed; temp_store=MEMORY so SQLite never writes temporary files elsewhere; no loadable extensions; secure_delete on; the run directory deleted when the run ends; and a crash-kept directory expiring under the existing 24-hour TTL, which is recorded as the accepted window for plaintext context on disk after a crash. orceld's redaction of secrets is unchanged and still applies before anything reaches the agent.

decisions.question: Rule change: the agent source scan grows by named imports only
decisions.decision: The M1 scan (apps/orcel-agent/tests/test_agent.py, SourceBoundary) admits standard-library imports only, forbids open() outside journal.py and allows one spawn (the edge). Slices extend it only by name: slice 2 adds langchain_core and langchain (agents, middleware, chat-model and message modules); slice 3 nothing beyond copied files; slice 4 the LangChain middleware modules; slice 5 langgraph, langgraph.checkpoint.sqlite and sqlite3 in one named store module, and ctypes in one named Windows-ACL module that may call only named advapi32 and kernel32 functions (security-descriptor, ACL and CreateDirectoryW calls), pinned by name in the scan. A denylist is added and never narrowed: mcp.client, mcp.server, langchain_mcp_adapters.client and .sessions, ClientSession, stdio_client, langchain_community, any provider SDK (langchain_openai, langchain_anthropic, langchain_ollama and similar), subprocess outside edge.py, socket, urllib, http.client and enable_load_extension. Every addition is made in the slice that needs it and noted in its review.

decisions.question: Dependency admission corrections
decisions.decision: mcp and langchain-mcp-adapters are not admitted in slice 1: the M1 stdlib client keeps the edge session, and langchain-mcp-adapters cannot convert tools without opening its own session, so slice 2 converts the edge's tool schemas itself unless it records a need and a review. Licenses expected outside the permissive allowlist are recorded now for review in slice 1, not admitted by default: certifi (MPL-2.0, used unmodified, file-level copyleft). A package with a native SQLite loadable extension (for example sqlite-vec) is excluded or, if a dependency requires it, never loaded (enable_load_extension stays off). The advisory auditor (pip-audit) is itself installed from a hash-pinned lock.

decisions.question: Egress denial
decisions.decision: The tracer variables are set to off in the agent's entry point before any LangChain or LangGraph import: LANGSMITH_TRACING, LANGCHAIN_TRACING_V2, LANGCHAIN_TRACING, LANGSMITH_ENDPOINT and LANGCHAIN_ENDPOINT cleared, LANGSMITH_API_KEY and LANGCHAIN_API_KEY cleared, OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=true and OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=none. Tests install a sys.addaudithook before any import that refuses socket.connect, socket.getaddrinfo and socket.gethostbyname, and the Linux CI leg also runs the agent's tests in a network namespace without a route (sudo unshare -n, available on hosted runners, dropping back to the runner's own user and groups inside the namespace with setpriv so the owner-only store tests are not run as root, and asserting the tests did not run as root); the leg fails if that cannot run.

decisions.question: Lease precondition in tests
decisions.decision: Every run through a real orceld starts it from a fresh, empty test state root and asserts before the run that no Full User or Admin lease exists there (the lease store is empty).

decisions.question: Scope mapping: task decomposition
decisions.decision: The directive's "Todo and task-decomposition middleware" is slice 4's todos item: LangChain's TodoListMiddleware is the decomposition mechanism DeerFlow extends. Subagent delegation (DeerFlow's subagents/executor.py) stays M6.

decisions.question: Slice 1 findings (recorded with slice 1, before merge)
decisions.decision: Resolving the lock on the pin's versions found: (1) orjson 3.11.8 is "MPL-2.0 AND (Apache-2.0 OR MIT)" (it vendors MPL-2.0 files); it is admitted as a second recorded license exception beside certifi (MPL-2.0), both used unmodified, and tools/licenses.py admits each only with exactly that expression. (2) The advisory audit reported GHSA-3fx2-cqw9-xr3c (CVE-2026-118667) in langgraph-sdk 0.4.4, the pin's version; it is moved to the fixed 0.4.6, inside langgraph 1.2.9's range (>=0.4.2,<0.5.0), and recorded in apps/orcel-agent/requirements-notes.md; the agent never uses the SDK's HTTP client. (3) langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite requires sqlite-vec 0.1.9, a native SQLite extension that only langgraph.store.sqlite loads; the agent never imports langgraph.store (on the denylist) and the egress test refuses the sqlite3 enable_load_extension and load_extension audit events. (4) urllib3 binds a throwaway socket to loopback port 0 at import to detect IPv6 (urllib3/util/connection.py, _has_ipv6), catching any failure. The egress hook refuses it like every other bind, so urllib3 assumes no IPv6; the test tolerates exactly those refused attempts (the AF_INET6 socket creation matched by family, and the loopback port-0 bind matched by address, each also by file and function) and fails on any other. No listener or connection results. (5) ctypes is not on the never-narrowed denylist, because slice 5 may admit it in one named Windows-ACL module; it stays outside the import allowlist until then. Review round 1 additions: (6) the agent source scan admits sys (quiet.py refuses with TracingAlreadyImported if langsmith was imported first, because it caches its environment), and its denylist grows (private socket and SSL modules, mail and FTP clients, socketserver, xmlrpc, webbrowser, asyncio connection and server names, and denied names inside string constants) above a floor the test ties to this spec's scan decision. (7) The egress hook also refuses socket creation, sendto, sendmsg, getnameinfo, process spawns and ctypes.dlopen, reports at exit after langsmith's flush, and has a negative control: without the agent's import the same environment turns tracing on and the hook must record langsmith's attempt. (8) Residual risk, recorded: audit hooks do not see network calls made from C code that bypasses Python's socket module; the Linux leg's network namespace blocks such calls but does not detect them, and on Windows and macOS only the hooks apply. The native packages in the lock (orjson, ormsgpack, xxhash, zstandard, uuid-utils, pydantic-core, sqlite-vec) contain no network code. (9) The universal lock keeps hashes for wheels of other Python versions (pip on 3.12 can select only cp312, abi3 or py3 wheels), every hash the donor lock records is present, and the lock is regenerable from the committed constraints-donor-pin.txt. (10) apps/orcel-agent/third_party/ is exempt from line-ending conversion (.gitattributes) so the MIT notice's SHA-256 holds on every checkout. (11) License readings without an SPDX expression are keyed on the exact version and raw License field reviewed. (12) The orcel-agent CI job is not a required status check; the exact-head gate is kept by merging a slice only when every check at its exact head, the agent job included, has passed. (13) Any later tolerance in the egress hook (for example the asyncio event loop's internal socketpair, once a slice runs async code) must be matched like the urllib3 one, by event, family or address, file and function, and recorded; a general loopback or socket exemption is never added. No other rule changes.

decisions.question: Slice 2 changes (recorded with slice 2, before merge)
decisions.decision: (1) The source scan admits third-party imports per module, keyed by the path inside orcel_agent/: langchain_core and langsmith in chat_planner.py only (langsmith goes beyond the scan decision's slice 2 list and is used only for its tracing_context, to switch tracing off); every other module keeps the standard-library allowlist, and the denylist is unchanged. (2) The gate's argument check (agent.py, arguments_match) is strengthened, not relaxed: besides required names, a proposal is refused before dispatch when an argument's JSON type does not match the tool's declared type (a boolean is never an integer) or when it names a property a closed schema (additionalProperties false) does not declare. It checks top-level types only (not nested objects, arrays, enum, anyOf or $ref); orceld validates fully. (3) ToolSpec gains the edge's tool description (capped at 2000 characters), so a model sees what the edge says each tool does. (4) A model reply that is neither exactly one tool call nor a finish becomes MalformedProposal, which the agent refuses (proposal-malformed); a model cannot batch calls. (5) Until slice 4's tool-output budget, each tool result is cut to 16000 characters before the model sees it. (6) orcel_agent/entry.py chat_agent is the way to build an agent for a chat-model planner and refuses any allowlist that is not a subset of the M1 read-only set; the Agent class itself still takes any allowlist so its unit tests can exercise mutating tools against a fake edge. (7) BM-02 Tier A parity runs each planned call through a scripted in-process chat model and the ChatModelPlanner and requires the parsed proposal to equal the planned call before dispatch; rows are labelled deterministic / orcel-agent-langchain-scripted. Review round 1 additions: (8) Read-only is enforced three times, independently: chat_agent takes only explicit options (no pass-through) and sets the agent's read_only_only flag; the gate then refuses, in prepare() and every dispatch, any allowlist or call outside READ_ONLY_TOOLS whatever was changed on the agent afterwards; and ChatModelPlanner refuses to run when offered, or asked to propose, any tool outside READ_ONLY_TOOLS. In-process code that rewrites the agent's private state is trusted code and out of scope. (9) Tracing: each model call also resets LangChain's own tracer variable (tracing_v2_callback_var, which takes priority over langsmith's context), and a model carrying callbacks of its own is refused; the test checks the run's actual handlers under tracing_v2_enabled(). (10) A step rebuilt from the journal after a resume is shown as 'RESULT NOT KEPT' with no arguments, not as an empty successful call; refusal codes reach the model only if they match [A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,63}, otherwise as INTERNAL_ERROR. (11) A tool the edge lists without an object input schema is dropped (fail closed). (12) The BM-02 chat mode dispatches the planner's own proposal, after checking the model was bound the edge's schema for the tool and the proposal equals the planned call; CI compares the chat report with M1's row by row (tests/benchmarks/compare_agent_reports.py), ignoring only latency. (13) Test changes: the slice 1 tracing-switch test runs in a fresh interpreter (a suite that has imported langsmith rightly makes silence_tracing() refuse), and the 'no MCP library' assertion is labelled a smoke check (the source scan is the guard). Review round 2 additions: (14) the callback refusal is repeated on every call, for the model and for the bound model's config; (15) resumed steps carry an explicit Step.resumed flag set by Agent.prepare(), so a resumed call with genuinely empty arguments is not shown as a real result; (16) the gate flag is private (_read_only_only) and set only by chat_agent; (17) the parity comparison fails on duplicate case keys, and the slice 2 acceptance now names exactly what it compares; (18) a chat-model planner cannot spend an approval (it is read-only), so the gate's approval-budget and stop-at-denial rules are proven by M1's gate tests, unchanged. No other rule changes.

decisions.question: Slice 3: loop detection, and keeping the M1 loop (architecture change, recorded before merge)
decisions.decision: (1) Architecture change from the master plan, row 1. Row 1 said to reimplement a thin loop on LangChain's create_agent with the copied middlewares. create_agent owns its loop and executes tools in its own tool node, so the M1 gate's rules (the step budget, refusal-is-final, the stop at an approval denial, the approval budget and the resume invariant with OUTCOME_UNKNOWN) would have to be re-created inside a tool callback, outside the loop that enforces them today, and every create_agent upgrade could change how they hold. The agent therefore keeps the M1 loop as the only dispatcher, and DeerFlow middlewares are adapted to run through ChatModelPlanner rather than as AgentMiddleware on a LangGraph graph. Later slices follow the same rule: a LangChain or DeerFlow component may shape what the model sees or how its reply is read, but never executes a tool. Downside, recorded: the packet's rows 3 and 4 (LangChain's TodoListMiddleware and SummarizationMiddleware) can no longer be plain REUSE through create_agent; slice 4 adapts their behaviour through the planner in the same way. (2) Loop detection is ADAPT (copied logic, adapted integration): orcel_agent/loop_detection.py keeps DeerFlow's argument normalisation, read-range window, per-tool keys, order-independent call-set hash, both detection layers, warn-once and the decision record unchanged in logic; it maps DeerFlow's tool names to the Orcel edge's (read_file to fs_read and fs_read_range, whose max_lines becomes the end line; write_file and str_replace to fs_write and fs_edit; bash, ls, glob and grep to fs_list, fs_find and fs_search), drops the LangGraph runtime scoping, LRU, fallback run ids and lock (one detector per run), replaces the middleware hooks with ChatModelPlanner calls, rewrites the wrap-up text for a read-only agent, and records decisions in the agent's EventLog. The provenance ledger and the donor lock record the source, blob and every modification. (3) Integration: a queued warning reaches the next model call as one static Orcel message after the tool messages (DeerFlow's wrap_model_call placement); a hard stop ends the run as a Finish with stop_reason loop_capped, so the looping call is never dispatched. Defaults are DeerFlow's: warn at 3 identical calls, stop at 5, window 20, per-tool frequency warn 30 and stop 50. (4) Tests: DeerFlow's tests of the detection core are ported, rewritten against LoopDetector with Orcel names, each naming its original; its tests of run and thread scoping, LRU eviction, fallback run ids, threading, run events, config loading and graph integration have no counterpart because the adapted detector has none of that machinery. A loop-trap test through the gate shows the warning, the hard stop, the decisions in the event log and that the fifth identical call is never dispatched. (5) The source scan admits collections (standard library) in loop_detection.py only. Review round 1 additions: (6) a loop-capped finish is reported, not hidden: Finish and RunResult carry stop_reason 'loop_capped' and the run.finished event records it. (7) Detection is on by default (ChatModelPlanner builds a LoopDetector unless detect_loops=False), a new goal resets it, and the BM-02 chat mode keeps one planner per episode; loop history is in memory, so it does not survive a resume (slice 5's checkpoints may change that). (8) The warning queue follows DeerFlow exactly: deduplicated, newest four kept, merged deduplicated into one message named 'loop_warning', restored to the front when a model call fails. (9) Read keys follow the edge: an omitted max_lines is the edge's default of 200 lines, and workspace_id joins the key. (10) The per-tool frequency defaults are scaled to the 32-step budget (warn 12, stop 20; DeerFlow's 30 and 50 could never fire within it); the identical-call defaults stay DeerFlow's (3, 5, window 20). (11) The narration-stripping rule has no effect on the Orcel fs tools (they take no description argument and closed schemas refuse one) and is kept only for faithfulness. (12) Every DeerFlow detection-core test is ported or listed with its reason in the test module. Review round 2 additions: (13) loop history also resets after any finish, so a planner reused for a second run with the same goal starts fresh; (14) expected false positive, recorded: paging one large file in more than 20 fs_read_range calls is real progress but is loop_capped by the per-tool limit at the default 12/20, the same trade-off DeerFlow makes at its own scale; (15) a capped run's outcome is still 'finished', so slice 6 and BM-02 scoring must read stop_reason (see the slice 6 acceptance). No other rule changes.

decisions.question: Evaluation labels
decisions.decision: Every SG-000129 benchmark row is labelled deterministic-scripted (a fake chat model replaying a plan or the tasks' scripted plans). No row is presented as autonomous model performance; that needs M4's model decision.

decisions.question: M3 slice 4a1: memory-only output preview budget
decisions.decision: Replaces the model-facing slice 2 16000-character prefix truncation with a bounded head/tail preview (16000 Unicode code points per tool message, metadata included) and a counts-only JSON shape hint. The full Step.result is unchanged in process; only the conversation ToolMessage is previewed. No output is stored or sent, and no tool, permission, approval or dependency is added. The preview is untrusted text, not a receipt. Failure, OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and resumed results keep their existing deterministic notices. Every Orcel-synthesized preview line starts with a marker (U+27E6 'Orcel' U+27E7) and any occurrence of that marker in tool output is replaced with a quoted form, so a result cannot reproduce Orcel's exact marker (look-alike characters are not caught, and the preview stays untrusted data; a real value containing the marker reaches the model quoted). The shape hint and preview_source_chars describe the quoted text actually previewed. Provenance, corrected in review: this is a REIMPLEMENTATION with DeerFlow's tool-output budget as design reference only (no code copied, so no provenance-ledger entry); the packet's row 5 said ADAPT the budget and COPY the synopsis, and the synopsis is deliberately not copied because it renders keys and sample values into a synthesized preview, which would put tool-controlled text into Orcel's framing. Consequently 4a1 ports no DeerFlow output-budget tests. The aggregate size of the conversation is not bounded here (32 steps of 16000 code points is about 512000) and is deferred to compaction (4c); the limit counts code points, not model tokens. Origin: implemented by another assistant session (PR #542) and handed over; reviewed and corrected by a fresh-context judge. 4a1 does not implement the remaining 4a error handling, 4b todos or 4c compaction.

decisions.question: M3 slice 4a2: typed failures, unknown outcomes and planner errors (recorded before merge)
decisions.decision: (1) A failed or refused call reaches the model as an error-status tool message carrying only orceld's typed FailureCode and static Orcel guidance for it (orcel_agent/failures.py); the error message, which comes from the call's target, never reaches the model. Every FailureCode in crates/orcel-contracts has guidance (a test reads the enum); an unknown or malformed code is INTERNAL_ERROR. The guidance never widens anything: a refusal stays final for the exact call (the gate enforces it), and no text invites approval, a lease or a retry of the same call. (2) An exception of any kind from the edge during a call (not only EdgeError) leaves the outcome unknown: it is journalled as OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, kept in the run's steps so the caller sees it, and the run stops (edge-failure); the M1 resume invariant still refuses to replay an unknown mutation. (3) An exception from the planner or the model stops the run as planner-error instead of crashing it; nothing is dispatched. (4) Conversation pairing (chat_planner.ensure_paired): every tool call is followed by its result and every result follows its call; a call with no result gets a synthetic OUTCOME_UNKNOWN error result (never a made-up success) and a result whose call is gone is dropped. It changes nothing today (the conversation is built in pairs) and is what compaction (4c) relies on. (5) Provenance: design reference only, no code copied, from DeerFlow's tool_error_handling_middleware.py and dangling_tool_call_middleware.py (both in the donor lock). Their LangGraph tool-node wrapping, skill metadata and id relabelling do not apply: Orcel's gate is the only dispatcher and builds the conversation itself. Review round 1 additions: (6) codes orceld returns after the operation may already have run (POSTCONDITION_FAILED, PROCESS_TIMEOUT, PROCESS_TERMINATION_UNVERIFIED, OUTPUT_LIMIT) are not called 'refused': the model is told the call may have acted, and the gate treats such a mutation like an unknown outcome (never replayed, a fresh observation owed), in dispatch and on resume; OUTPUT_LIMIT's text covers both a too-large result and a too-large request. (7) Every refusal tells the model that proposing the same call again ends the run (repeat-refused). (8) An edge failure or a planner error keeps the run's store (it is resumable like a crash, and the journal holds the unknown outcome resume must not replay); a clean finish or any other stop still deletes it. (9) ensure_paired gives each result to one call only (a later call reusing an id gets the synthetic unknown result, never the earlier success) and refuses a tool call without a string id; invalid_tool_calls are excluded because propose refuses a reply carrying them. (10) run.stopped context: the exception type (never its message) is recorded for edge failures and planner errors. No other rule changes.

decisions.question: M3 slice 4b: todos, completion reminders and clarification (recorded before merge)
decisions.decision: (1) Todos and clarification are planner-internal. ChatModelPlanner offers two internal tools, write_todos and ask_clarification, beside the edge's read-only tools; neither is ever dispatched to the edge, journalled as an Orcel call or counted against the step budget, and an edge tool with either name is refused. (2) write_todos updates an in-memory list (at most 20 items of at most 300 characters, statuses pending, in_progress or completed; an invalid list is refused with an error result and the plan unchanged). The list is shown at each later proposal as a reminder labelled as the model's own notes, written from untrusted data, that authorize nothing. A todo cannot widen anything: only a real tool call through the planner's read-only check and the gate can act. (3) Finishing while todos are incomplete is answered with DeerFlow's completion reminder at most twice per run, then the finish is accepted. (4) ask_clarification ends the run with the question (at most 1000 characters) as the answer and stop_reason needs_clarification; a question is never consent. (5) A proposal may make at most 4 model calls (todo updates and reminders happen inside it); more is a malformed proposal. Planning is on by default (planning=False turns it off) and resets with each run. The plan is in memory and does not survive a resume (slice 5 checkpoints may change that). (6) Provenance: COPY, verbatim, of LangChain's write_todos description, system prompt and Todo TypedDict (MIT, third_party/langchain/), copied rather than imported because importing langchain.agents.middleware.todo loads the agent factory, LangGraph's runtime and websockets; COPY from DeerFlow's todo_middleware.py of _format_todos, _has_tool_call_intent_or_error, the two-reminder cap and the length-truncation skip; ADAPT of its context-loss and completion reminders; DeerFlow's clarification middleware is a design reference only. The ledger, donor lock and file header record it. (7) Rule change: the source scan admits langchain_core in todos.py only (the earlier scan decision's 'LangChain middleware modules' for slice 4 is not used: the todo text is copied instead). Review round 1 additions: (8) the todo list is replayed in the tool channel (a write_todos call and its result), never as a message in the person's voice; todo content and questions may not contain control characters or angle brackets, so they cannot carry markup that breaks out of the untrusted label. (9) The completion reminder is labelled untrusted and no longer says 'must'; a finish with todos still open after the reminders carries stop_reason todos_incomplete, so it is not a clean finish. (10) An answer on the last internal turn is accepted, not reminded, so the turn bound can no longer turn a real answer into a malformed proposal; a write_todos on the last turn is the only way to hit the bound. (11) The model's write_todos call ids are rewritten (todo-N) so they never collide with conversation ids. Review round 2 additions: (12) todo content and questions also refuse Unicode control, format (including bidi overrides) and line/paragraph separator characters and angle-bracket look-alikes (questions may keep newlines); the scan admits unicodedata (standard library) in todos.py for this. (13) A refused write_todos list is not echoed back to the model, only that it was refused. (14) A finish whose content is a list of text blocks keeps its text. No other rule changes.

decisions.question: M3 slice 4c: context compaction and summarization (recorded before merge)
decisions.decision: (1) Once the rendered tool results pass 60000 characters, every step but the 6 most recent is compacted. Each older step keeps its call (arguments capped at about 400 characters) and its result: a success's result is replaced by a fixed notice; a refusal, an unknown outcome or a resumed step keeps its exact text, so refusal and unknown-outcome evidence is never summarized away. Pairing is untouched (every call keeps its result; ensure_paired still runs). (2) The successful results that are dropped are summarized by the same model in a separate call with no tools bound and tracing off, using LangChain's DEFAULT_SUMMARY_PROMPT copied verbatim; the summarizer sees only the previous summary and the newly dropped successful results (each previewed to 2000 characters), never the system prompt or failures. The summary is capped at 4000 characters, labelled as written from untrusted data that authorizes nothing, and placed on the last compacted tool result (the tool channel, never the person's voice). It is updated incrementally and cached; each compaction point is summarized at most once, and a failed summary falls back to the step records alone (the run does not stop). (3) Bounds (restated in review): the conversation holds the 6 most recent steps verbatim (each result previewed to 16000 characters, with uncapped arguments), one summary of at most 4000 characters and at most 26 compacted records (32 steps less the 6 recent), each with arguments capped at about 400 characters. Once compaction starts, each proposal may make one extra summarizer call whose input is the previous summary and at most 8 dropped successes previewed to 2000 characters each (about 20000 characters). (4) Nothing is stored or sent: the summary is in the planner's memory for the run, resets with each run and does not survive a resume (slice 5). Compaction is on by default (compaction=False turns it off). (5) Provenance: COPY, verbatim, of LangChain 1.3.14's DEFAULT_SUMMARY_PROMPT (MIT; third_party/langchain/NOTICE.md records the source file's SHA-256; the module is not imported); DeerFlow's summarization and durable-context middlewares are a design reference only, no code copied (their PII redaction, extension API, notifications and LangGraph state do not apply). Review round 1 additions: (6) every non-success (refusal, may-have-acted code, OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, resumed step) keeps exactly the text it had before compaction, from one shared function (failures.non_success_text), so a resumed step keeps its 'Observe again'. (7) Summarizer cost is bounded: at most one call per proposal, over at most 8 dropped successes (the rest folded in by later calls); after 2 failed summaries a run stops summarizing and keeps the records alone; a span with no successes needs no call. (8) The summarizer call starts with an Orcel system message that gives the person's goal and says everything in the results is untrusted data, never instructions, and that goals, instructions or next steps must not come from it; the summary's label says it was written by a summarizer model, not by the planner. A summarizer reply that carries tool calls is rejected. (9) The summary is always bounded and marker-neutralized, and Orcel's compaction notice and summary label start with the Orcel marker, so a tool result cannot reproduce them. (10) The size estimate counts capped arguments, and the knobs are validated (keep_recent at least 1, so the newest result is never compacted; trigger_chars at least 16000). No other rule changes.

invariants: orceld remains the sole execution and approval authority; the agent only proposes calls over MCP stdio to the Orcel edge.
The agent spawns exactly one child process, the built edge, and opens no socket or listener.
Every dispatch passes the M1 gate: the read-only allowlist, the step budget, the per-run approval budget (default 3, stop at the first denial), refusal-is-final and the resume invariant.

A mutating call dispatched but not recorded is surfaced as OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and is never re-dispatched from agent state; a read-only one may be repeated only as a re-observation, and the planner must re-observe before proposing any mutation.
Tool results, file and page text, summaries, todos and checkpoints are untrusted data; the system prompt is static Orcel text.
A model's finish is a claim, not a receipt; completion is judged from orceld results and task checkers.
Agent state lives only in the private per-run store: owner-only, size-capped, expiring, deleted when the run ends.
No DeerFlow sandbox, shell, file, browser, computer-control, gateway, telemetry or skill-install code is imported.
Every copied or adapted file names its DeerFlow path and the pin, and the verbatim MIT license ships beside it.
No model weights, tokenizer files or other runtime downloads; tests run with egress denied.
acceptance: Slice 1: the lock installs with pip --require-hashes --only-binary :all: --no-deps on Windows, macOS and Linux with Python 3.12; the license table covers every installed distribution and admits only the allowlist or a recorded, reviewed exception; the hash-pinned advisory audit reports no unaddressed advisory; importing the agent and its dependencies under the audit hook makes no connect or name lookup; LangSmith and OpenTelemetry tracing stay off when the environment asks for them; no tiktoken, provider SDK, mcp or langchain-mcp-adapters is installed; the provenance ledger and the verbatim MIT text (checked by hash) are complete.

Slice 2: the LangChain adapter, driven by an in-process fake chat model, solves BM-02 Tier A through the real edge and a fresh test orceld (no lease) on all three OSes with report rows identical to M1's except latency (case, status, observed result and step counts; compared in CI); the gate refuses before dispatch an invented tool, a tool outside the allowlist, schema-invalid arguments, an extra approval-bearing call and a call after a denial; the entry point refuses an allowlist that is not a subset of the M1 read-only set; the extended source scan and its denylist pass, and the only edge session is the M1 client's.
Slice 3: the ported loop-detection tests pass with Orcel tool names; a loop trap stops at the hard limit and the decision is recorded.

Slice 4: ported todo, summarization, output-budget, error and dangling-call tests pass; a summary or todo containing an instruction cannot add a tool or widen an argument; an oversized result is budgeted in memory or in the private store only; a dangling call after compaction is still OUTCOME_UNKNOWN.

Slice 5: resuming from a checkpoint drops any pending tool-call writes (LangGraph does not re-run them); killing the agent between dispatch and recording, with a test-only mutating tool on a fake edge (as M1's tests do), then resuming yields OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and no re-dispatch of that call, and with the real edge a re-observation before any further proposal; the checkpoint database and every SQLite sidecar stay inside the run directory and the size cap, and filling past the cap fails closed, temp_store is MEMORY, no extension loads, and the directory expires and is deleted on completion; the directory is owner-only from creation: mode 0700 on Unix, and on Windows created with a protected (inheritance-off) owner-only DACL through CreateDirectoryW with a security descriptor, tested for protection and for no broad principal.

Slice 6: a report comparing M2/M3 with M1 on BM-02 Tier A and the synthetic tasks, run against a fresh test orceld with no lease (asserted), with success, Orcel calls and refusals, approval requests, p50 and p95 step and task time, peak RSS, context size over time, loop and compaction events, resume outcomes and any security failure; every row labelled deterministic-scripted; a run whose stop_reason is set (for example loop_capped) is never counted as a clean success.
Every slice: the agent source scan, the egress-denied test and the M1 tests still pass; the agent is not packaged and not referenced by orceld.
Exact-head CI (Windows, macOS and Linux legs), Review Gates where they run, and a fresh-context security judge pass on each slice; d1-local is advisory only.
